intro: Fully funded 4-year PhD programme 2027 at The Francis Crick Institute London. £27,715 per year tax-free stipend, tuition covered for international students. Deadline: 3 November 2026, 12:00 midday GMT.
description:
Programme Overview

The Francis Crick Institute in London is recruiting doctoral candidates for its 2027 PhD programme. The Crick is one of the largest biomedical research institutes in Europe, and its students work alongside research groups spanning cancer, immunology, neuroscience, infection, and the physics and chemistry of living systems. Rather than choosing a single project in isolation, students join a four-year programme that starts with rotations and taught elements before settling into the thesis lab.

Every PhD student at the Crick registers with one of its partner universities, so the final degree comes from a UK institution while the day-to-day research happens inside the Crick's labs on Midland Road, next to St Pancras station. The institute currently hosts more than 200 PhD students and doctoral clinical fellows, and around 60% of them come from the EU and further afield, which makes this one of the more international biomedical PhD environments in the UK.

Three Ways Into the 2027 Programme

Recruitment routes and who they are for
RouteWho can apply
PhD student recruitmentOpen to everyone with the right academic background; the standard route into the 2027 intake.
Future Leaders in Biomedical Sciences ScholarshipsReserved for candidates of Black or mixed Black heritage; successful applicants receive the same Crick PhD place and studentship.
Doctoral clinical fellow recruitmentOpen to clinicians who want to combine clinical training with laboratory research.

Funding and Support

What the studentship pays
ComponentDetails
Stipend£27,715 per year, tax-free (living allowance), paid for the full four years.
Tuition feesCovered in full, including the international fee rate for students from outside the UK.
Research costsLab and project running costs are supported by the institute.
RegistrationDegree registration with a Crick partner university.

Application Dates

Key dates for the 2027 intake
ComponentDetails
StatusRecruitment open when checked on 22 October 2026
Deadline3 November 2026, 12:00 midday GMT
StartPhD programme starts in autumn 2027
LocationThe Francis Crick Institute, 1 Midland Road, London NW1 1AT

How to Apply

Applications go through the Crick's academic recruitment system, not by email. Candidates pick their route (standard PhD recruitment, Future Leaders scholarship, or clinical fellow) and submit their academic record, references and supporting statements before the midday deadline on 3 November. Because the deadline is a hard midday cut-off rather than the usual end-of-day, it is worth submitting a day or two early.

About The Francis Crick Institute

The Crick is a partnership between the Medical Research Council, Cancer Research UK and Wellcome, and it describes itself as a discovery laboratory focused on understanding the biology underlying human health and disease. For applicants deciding between a university lab and an institute, the practical difference is scale: shared facilities, on-site imaging, genomics and proteomics platforms, and a large doctoral community under one roof in central London.
